newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian firms have heavy tax debts - official.
newsitem.headline: Russian firms have heavy tax debts - official.

text.p: A senior Russian tax official called on Monday for legislation to be amended to help force companies to pay up trillions of roubles in tax arrears.
Vladimir Popov, head of the State Tax Service's department for enforcing penalties for companies in arrears, said the state's hands were tied when it tried to make debtors pay up.
"We can do it more effectively, but for that to happen existing legislation needs to be amended," he told a news conference.

Popov said total tax arrears of 155.2 trillion roubles on May 1 included 82.4 trillion roubles owed to the federal government, of which about 40 percent was owed by only 83 enterprises with tax debts of over 100 billion roubles each.

Popov named automobile producer Avtovaz, which owed 2.8 trillion roubles on April 1, and oil companies Yuganskneftegaz, which owes 1.7 trillion roubles, and Nizhnevartovskneftegaz, which owes 1.3 trillion roubles, among the biggest debtors.
But these debts are dwarfed by the 15 trillion roubles owed by subsidiaries of natural gas producer Gazprom.

Tax revenues, which totalled only 69 percent of targets in the first quarter of this year, are one of the government's most pressing problems, but Popov was sceptical that government efforts to date to raise tax revenues would bring results.

He said an emergency tax commission set up last autumn to deal with low tax collection rates had so far accomplished very little and said that the government's long-delayed tax code would be useless without economic growth.
"The tax code by itself is solving nothing and will solve nothing; everything has to be coordinated with economic reform," he said.

He said companies seeking to avoid paying taxes were making life difficult for tax officials by doing everything from registering at "legal" addresses rather than at their actual address to having multiple bank accounts.
